scope: Cross-cutting collections gathering anti-colonial and anti-feudal rebellions. Seeded with the long-arc rebellions collection; tribal-only and peasant-only sub-collections queued.

collections.title: Rebellions before and beyond 1857
collections.subtitle: Sannyasi-Fakir, Vellore, Paika, Kol, Khasi, Khond, Santhal, Birsa Munda, Heraka and others — the long arc of subcontinental anti-colonial revolt the textbook telling tends to compress into one date.
collections.summary: 1857 was not the first. Tribal, peasant, sepoy, Dalit, and religious-agrarian revolts ran continuously from the 1763 Sannyasi-Fakir raids in Bengal to the 1951 Telangana Rebellion against the Nehru government. This collection gathers the events that surface that long arc — the rebellions textbooks compress, displace, or omit.
collections.framing: Reading the corpus chronologically reveals a structure the canonical 'first war of independence in 1857' framing obscures. The Sannyasi-Fakir Rebellion runs from 1763 through the 1820s. The Vellore Mutiny (1806) anticipates 1857's sepoy grievances by half a century. Paika 1817, Kol 1831–32, Khasi 1829–33, Khond risings from 1837, the Faraizi Movement, and the Santhal Hool of 1855–56 all predate 1857 by years to decades. Post-1857 the chain continues: Indigo 1859, Birsa Munda 1899–1900, Champaran 1917, Moplah 1921, Rampa 1922–24, the Mahad and Vaikom satyagrahas of the 1920s, Heraka under Jadonang and Rani Gaidinliu 1929–32, and the Communist-led Telangana Rebellion that fought past Indian independence into 1951. Many were tribal (Khasi, Kol, Khond, Santhal, Birsa, Heraka, Telangana — tagged also as `tribal`); several were peasant agrarian (Faraizi, Indigo, Champaran, Moplah, Telangana — tagged `peasant`); two were caste-rights satyagrahas (Vaikom, Mahad — tagged `caste-rights`). Lakshmibai's 1857 letters stand in for the rebellion of 1857 itself until that event is authored as its own entry.
